# Stand Firm in the Gap
## Scripture
"Watch, stand fast in the faith, be brave, be strong." – 1 Corinthians 16:13

## Reflection
Brother, the world tells you that strength is about muscle, money, or influence. But Paul's command to the church in Corinth cuts through the noise: *Watch. Stand fast. Be brave. Be strong.* This isn't a suggestion—it's a battle order. You are called to be a sentinel, not a slumberer. To stand fast means your feet are planted on the Rock, not shifting sand. It means your convictions aren't swayed by the latest cultural winds or the opinions of the crowd. Being brave isn't the absence of fear; it's moving forward with the fear of God outweighing the fear of man. And being strong isn't self-reliance—it's the quiet, stubborn dependence on the Holy Spirit that says, "I can't, but He can." Today, you will face a gap—a weakness in your marriage, a challenge at work, a temptation in your mind. Will you stand in that gap, or will you retreat? The Warrior of Christ doesn't retreat; he kneels in prayer, rises in faith, and holds the line.

## Daily Challenge
Identify one area where you've been drifting. Take a physical stand: stand at attention for 60 seconds, recite this verse aloud, and commit to holding that ground today. Then do 20 pushups as a reminder that your strength comes from the Lord.
